Good, the scope is settled. The next part is what happens after the first text goes out.

You said the seedlings have about two hours once the heater fails. With a 15-minute repeat, that is about eight texts. If the on-call person sleeps through all of them, or their phone is off, nobody acts in time. A common answer is to escalate: after a set number of unacknowledged texts, the alert also goes to a second person, or to everyone.

I also noticed a related risk. The alerts would run on the same machine as `ingest/`. A power cut or a crashed machine would stop both the readings and the alerts, and nobody would get a text. I'm not asking you to decide that now. I'll come back to it when we talk about where this runs.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- An alerting system has to report its own failures. Silence from a dead system looks the same as "all is well."
- The 10-minute stale-sensor alert covers one sensor going quiet. It cannot cover the alert service itself going quiet. That check usually has to come from outside the machine.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

If the on-call person doesn't acknowledge an alert, who should hear about it next, and how soon?
